problem: In PointNav without GPS+compass, wide-baseline frame pairs (0.25 m / 30 deg per action) break traditional geometric VO (drift, outlier matches on featureless walls, depth noise). Learned VO (Partsey et al.) works but needs huge datasets and compute.
motivation: Reliable VO is a drop-in replacement for GPS+compass in noisy PointNav (v2), and sample efficiency matters when target-domain data is scarce and costly. Motion priors that are already available during navigation (the action, a coarse geometric pose) can constrain both geometric and learned pose estimation.
key_idea: Use the agent's action prior to bias a training-free geometric coarse pose estimator, then feed both the action prior and the coarse pose (plus action-prior overlap-masked RGB-D) into a neural regressor that outputs the fine relative pose.
insight: Ablations show the coarse pose prior (CP) gives the largest gain at small data (50k: CP-only 57.79% SR vs AP-only 37.27%). Adding the action prior stabilizes training at larger data, where CP alone plateaus, and the action-prior overlap masks add further gains (50k: 54.70 -> 63.40 SR). The result is about 2x sample efficiency over Partsey et al. Standalone, action-prior-biased iterative re-weighting drastically cuts ATE versus unbiased SuperPoint+LightGlue/Teaser++ pipelines (58.80 vs 107.29 cm for the best baseline).
method: GCPE (Geometric Coarse Pose Estimator): SuperPoint keypoints, Lowe-ratio (NNSR) matching, top-m correspondences back-projected to 3D with depth; training-free.

Iterative prior-biased pose sampling: candidate SE(2) poses are sampled around the action prior, alternating rotation and translation samples; sigma is halved each iteration (initial 0.06 m, 0.06 m, 4 deg), and the best candidate becomes the next mean.

Motion-Prior Correspondence Weighting (MPCW): each 3D-3D match is weighted by inverse symmetric 3D endpoint error under the candidate pose, multiplied by the previous iteration's best weights. Candidate score is the sum of weights, and iteration stops on a score-improvement criterion.

NFPR (Neural Fine Pose Regression): ResNet-18 encoder, compression block and 3-layer MLP decoder (based on Partsey et al.). The raw action prior and coarse pose are concatenated after the first FC layer, and the action embedding is dropped.

Action-prior overlap masks (APOM): RGB and depth of each view are warped to the other view using the action prior and depth, and the input is masked to the overlapping region and stacked channel-wise.
Training data: a static dataset of (O_{t-1}, O_t, T_ap, T_cp, T_gt) from oracle shortest-path trajectories, with T_cp cached; MSE loss, Adam lr 1e-4, batch 128, 50 epochs.

Navigation: the estimated relative poses are integrated to update the goal coordinates, which feed a frozen pretrained DD-PPO-style depth-only policy (half-width ResNet-50 + 2-layer LSTM) from Partsey et al.

setting.backbone: GCPE (SuperPoint + geometric sampling, training-free) + NFPR (ResNet-18 + MLP, trained) for VO; frozen pretrained RL nav policy (ResNet-50 + LSTM) from Partsey et al.
setting.training_data: NFPR trained on 50k-400k RGB-D pairs sampled from oracle trajectories of PointNav v2 in the 72 Gibson 4+ train scenes; nav policy pretrained, not retrained
setting.observation: noisy egocentric RGB-D (depth only to the policy) plus previous action; no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: discrete: move_forward 0.25 m, turn_left/right 30 deg, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson scenes, PointNav v2 with noisy sensors and actuation)
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle agent with GT map used only to generate VO training data)

numbers_note: Benchmark is Gibson PointNav v2 (val split, 994 episodes); it is not in the canonical list, so it is reported as Gibson-PointNav. DTG is d_g in cm. The dataset-size table reports rounded success (50k 63, 100k 66, 200k 72, 400k 78 vs SoA 35, 60, 65, 72).
results: With 400k samples, GCPE+NFPR reaches 78.21% SR / 61.01 SPL versus 72.23 / 55.99 for Partsey et al. (SoA), with lower ATE (15.51 vs 19.09 cm). At 50k it reaches 63% SR vs 35% for SoA, and roughly matches SoA success with about half the data. The training-free GCPE alone beats SuperPoint+LightGlue+RWP (35.31 vs 28.77 SR).
limitations: Evaluated only in the Habitat/Gibson simulator on PointNav v2, with no real-robot experiments and no other tasks, although the paper suggests other tasks and motion priors (IMU, wheel odometry).

Depends on cached coarse poses from GCPE, whose sparse-feature matching is stochastic and fails on featureless walls. GCPE and NFPR are trained and tuned on the same simulated embodiment and dataset, so embodiment and dataset specificity is not addressed.
Ablations lack a full comparison against SoA at every data scale, and the SoA rows show rounded success. The paper trains on at most 400k samples.
